exact_source: Anastasia Kireeva, Randomstrasse 101, 2026-06-05, first displayed low-degree framework Open Problem 35

frozen_metric.name: E_framework
frozen_metric.movement_reason: A source-valid general sufficient framework was proved: in a finite graded Q-space with G-invariant planted and null laws and a reversible grade-contractive noise operator, bounded source low-degree advantage plus bounded expected null-defined invariant leverage tail implies a uniform total-variation gap from one after noise, hence no strong distinguisher of any degree; the condition applies to arbitrary fixed finite k-array product settings and is not a special Gaussian/vector/matrix theorem.

methods.B14: Defined the null/group/noise invariant leverage profile and proved the full chi-square/TV framework theorem.
methods.B6: Proved the k=1 versus k=2 symmetry boundary: d_j=1 for fully exchangeable vector coordinates, while graph-edge vertex symmetry has invariant dimension at least exp(j log j - 2 j log log j - O(j)), so fixed noise cannot control graph symmetry by dimension alone.
methods.B24: Proved that the worst G-invariant high-degree energy is attained by a single orbit law and that the leverage envelope is worst-case sharp degree by degree.
